g.text: ISA-L holds a higher clock here only because this run started 7 °C cooler.
In the reversed pass it ran at the same 167% as CNG and still sent 1809 MB/s
against CNG's 1618 — fewer cycles per byte is what carries it, not more clock.

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 14px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start

g.text: Two minutes of AES-128-GCM at line rate: throughput, temperature, clock
Each run encrypts 32 KB packets and sends them over raw TCP to the Linux box, which logged the same rates it received (within 1 MB/s).
The receiver never exceeded 7% CPU, so nothing here is the far end.
Windows: Dell Latitude 7490, i5-8350U (4 cores / 8 threads, 15 W) · Linux: Ryzen 7 PRO 7840U · Thunderbolt networking, MTU 65330, link 20 Gbit/s
AES-128-GCM as SSH uses it: one complete GCM message per 32 KB packet, fresh IV, 4 bytes of AAD, 16-byte tag, one thread
